answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with earned-reputation aging: a new identity starts at zero trust no matter how grand its fable of past deeds, and only verified completed work raises its standing over weeks. A raven that copies itself a thousand times gains nothing, because each copy restarts at zero and must pay the same slow cost in real work. Timber for the system is time itself: an attacker needs months of genuine service per identity, so flooding the network costs more than any fake vote or reward it could steal.
